Bob Burt Cabinets & Pedals browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Bob Burt GR8T Distortion Published on August 19, 2011 Bob Burt Cabinets & Pedals distortion pedal Information The Bob Burt GR8T Distortion is a hand-built pedal designed to deliver a wide spectrum of distortion tones, ranging from raw rock crunch to compressed, D-style overdrive. Unlike an overdrive circuit, where the op amp handles amplification directly, the GR8T generates distortion from gain stages positioned after the op amp, resulting in a different response to guitar volume and dynamics. This design gives the pedal a distinct feel and allows it to interact naturally with a player's touch. The GR8T is based around a single gain stage, which keeps the circuit quiet while maintaining clarity, note definition, and pure guitar tone. Central to the pedal's flexibility is an eight-position rotary switch that adjusts the amount of compression in gradual steps. Starting with no compression, each step clockwise increases compression and reshapes the distortion waveform, offering eight unique voices in one pedal. This approach avoids the complexity of multiple toggle switches and makes tonal recall easy. When combined with its gain, tone, and volume controls, the rotary switch allows the GR8T to move seamlessly between open, aggressive distortion suited to hard rock and metal, and smooth, compressed tones ideal for fusion or D-style overdrive sounds. The pedal responds well to adjustments in guitar volume, cleaning up naturally when rolled back. A precision Texas Instruments op amp was chosen for the circuit, selected as the closest modern equivalent to the LM308 chip found in some classic distortion pedals. As with all of Bob Burt's designs, premium components were used for low noise, tonal consistency, and reliability. The pedal is true bypass, built and tested by hand, and often finished with one-of-a-kind custom swirl paint jobs. Controls Level - Adjusts the overall output volume of the effect. Tone - Shapes the EQ balance of the distortion, ranging from darker to brighter tones. Gain - Sets the amount of distortion and sustain. 8-Way Rotary Switch - Introduces progressive compression in eight steps, altering the distortion character from raw and open to compressed and smooth.
